bodyHtml:
A decision guide to Protestchat: what it is for, when it fits, how to start, and which compatibility or maintenance details deserve a closer look.

Quick verdict

Encrypted messaging with no internet, no cell tower, and no server. Phones relay for each other over Bluetooth mesh, so it keeps working during internet shutdowns and inside cellular jammers

Shortlist Protestchat only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

Protestchat is most relevant to developers working with TypeScript. Its source topics point to bluetooth low energy, censorship resistance, e2ee, internet freedom. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Read the README, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license before cloning Protestchat. Start in a disposable environment that matches your runtime and deployment constraints.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 164 GitHub stars, 24 forks, 45 open issues, and last source push 2026-07-22.

The source reports the MIT license.

Stars, forks, and issue counts show repository activity or attention; they do not prove quality, security, or suitability.

Bottom line

Protestchat is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Start with the official repository

git clone https://github.com/ni5arga/protestchat

Read the repository documentation, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license before using the project. Try it in a disposable or non-production environment first.
